resources.title: Exploring your environment
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: 1. Things in and around the classroom, school and home. 2. Types of roads within and outside the school. 3. Walking along the road and crossing the road.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. observe and identify things in and around the classroom, school and home; 2. identify types of roads around the school and roads outside the school; 3. demonstrate walking along the road and crossing the road safely.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Takes pupils on a study walk around and outside the school. 2. Demonstrates walking safely along the road and crossing the road. 3. Encourages pupils to observe and list things in the home.

Students: 1. Pupils observe and list things in the school environment 2. Draw some of the things around the school 3. Demonstrate working safely along the road.
resources.resources: 1. Objects in the classroom, around the school and home 2. Charts and models 3. Drawing materials
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify things in and around the classroom, school and home; 2. sketch any two things identified in and around the classroom, school and home; 3. demonstrate how to walk and cross a road safely.

resources.title: Soil, Air and Water
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: Other parts of the surrounding( e.g. soil, water, air).
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify other parts of their surroundings – soil, air and water; 2. demonstrate that air exists; 3. create air current by blowing with the mouth or using paper fan; 4. demonstrate that air occupies space using balloons; 5. list the common sources of water.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to identify soil, air and water as other components of the surrounding. 2. Demonstrates the existence of air using paper or hand fan. 3. Demonstrates that air occupies space by inflating balloons. 4. Takes pupils on a tour of nearby water sources

Students: 1. Touch and feel soil in the playground. 2. Create air currents by blowing with the mouth or using hand or paper fan. 3. Inflate balloons, polythene bags etc. 4. Mention sources of water. 5. Recite a poem about water
resources.resources: 1. Soil 2. Newspaper 3. Paper fan 4. Hand fan 5. Balloons 6. Polythene bags. 7. Water 8. Pictures of sources of water.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify other parts of their surroundings; 2. show that air exists; 3. demonstrate that air occupies space; 4. name five common sources of water.

resources.title: Colour (identification)
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: 1. Colours of objects 2. Road traffic light signs 3. Road markings
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify different colours; 2. collect materials of different colours; 3. observe road traffic light and identify their colours; 4. State the function of each road traffic light sign; 5. identify road markings and their colours.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses the colour chart to guide pupils to identify colours. 2. Gives pupils different materials to identify different colours. 3. Separates colour using ‘lego’ materials with different colours for modelling. 4. Draws road traffic signs for pupils to observe. 5. Takes pupils to observe various road traffic signs in their location. 6. Supervises pupils in drawing and painting of road traffic signs.

Students: 1. Identify colours of objects provided by teacher. 2. Observe road traffic signs. 3. Match the colours of road traffic light with their functions.
resources.resources: 1. Flowers 2. Leaves 3. Colour 4. Containers of various colours 5. Lego sets/bricks
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify five colours; 2. identify various road traffic lights by their colours and functions; 3. identify some road traffic markings and their colours; 4. draw and colour road traffic lights.

resources.title: Living Things
resources.description: Theme: LIVING AND NON LIVING THINGS | Content: 1. Living things in the school environment. 2. Living things in the home.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify self as a living thing; 2. identify other living things in the classroom, school and at home.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses pictures and charts to guide pupils to identify living things in the school environment and home. 2. Guides pupils to explore the school surroundings identifying living things (to include themselves)

Students: 1. Identify from pictures and charts living things. 2. Identify self as a living thing 3. Identify other living things at school and home.
resources.resources: 1. Charts and pictures of animals and plants. 2. People in the classroom and in the school compound.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify self as a living thing; 2. identify living things in their classroom; 3. identify at least two living things outside their classroom.

resources.title: Non -Living things
resources.description: Theme: LIVING AND NON LIVING THINGS | Content: 1. Non- living things in the classroom, school and at home
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to identify non -living things in the classroom, in the school and at home.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses pictures and charts to identify non living things in the classroom, school and at home. 2. Guides them to identify non- living things in the classroom and school.

Students: 1. Identify from pictures and charts non-living things 2. Identify non- living things in the classroom and school. 3. Identify air, soil and water as non- living things.
resources.resources: 1. Objects in the classroom (chairs, desks, books, bags etc). 2. Water 3. Soil 4. paper
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify three non- living things in the classroom; 2. identify five non- living things around the school.

resources.title: Simple Machines
resources.description: Theme: UNDERSTANDING BASIC TECHNOLOGY | Content: 1. Meaning of: Simple machine (a device that makes work easy e.g. Broom, Spoon, See-saw/swing, Hoe, Cutlass etc.) 2. The safe use of simple machines.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify and collect simple machine in the school; 2. use simple machines in a safe way.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Provides samples of simple machines in the home and school. 2. Leads pupils to use some simple machines (broom, pair of scissors, see- saw/swing). 3. Demonstrates how to safely use simple machine.

Students: 1. Collect and use some simple machines e.g. broom, hoe, can- opener, spoon etc. 2. Play on a see- saw/swing. 3. Identify dangers in the use of simple machines.
resources.resources: 1. Brooms 2. See-saw 3. Hoe 4. Cutlass 5. Can opener 6. Spoon
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention three simple machines in the school; 2. demonstrate how to use some simple machines safely.

resources.title: Energy
resources.description: Theme: UNDERSTANDING BASIC TECHNOLOGY | Content: 1. Meaning of energy as exemplified by people doing some work. 2. Examples of things that use energy.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of energy; 2. perform activities involving the use of energy;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to identify themselves using energy to move, write, jump, run, lift objects etc. 2. Guides pupils using charts and posters to identify objects around them where energy is used e.g. grinding machine, pounding with mortar and pestle, riding a bicycle etc.

Students: 1. Perform simple activities showing the use of energy such as walking, running, jumping, and lifting an object. 2. Identify from charts and posters objects that show the use of energy
resources.resources: 1. Pupils in the classroom 2. Desks and chairs 3. Posters and charts
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. state the meaning of energy; 2. perform an action to show the use of energy; 3. list any three things that use energy to work.

resources.title: Moving our body parts
resources.description: Theme: BASIC MOVEMENTS | Content: 1. Leaping, Walking stepping, hopping and running etc. 2. Throwing of objects, catching of objects, kicking of objects, striking of objects etc. 3. Safety rules
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. demonstrate correct movement patterns of leaping, walking, stepping, hopping and running, etc; 2. perform basic manipulative movements; 3. identify safety rules in walking, running, pushing and kicking etc.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Demonstrates the technique in locomotor movement, 2. Supervises the pupils and offers assistance. 3. Demonstrates the non- locomotor movements, supervises the children and offers assistance. 4. Demonstrates the basic manipulative movements, supervise the children and offers assistance. 5. List safety rules in basic movements.

Students: 1. Practice the techniques of leaping, walking and running. 2. Practice non- locomotor movements 3. Practice manipulative patterns of:- throwing - catching in pairs. 4. List dangers in basic movements.
resources.resources: Playground, balls etc.
resources.assessment: Ask the pupils to: 1. demonstrate basic movement skills correctly; 2. mention safety rules on the playground.

resources.title: Athletics
resources.description: Theme: SPORTS ANDGAMES | Content: 1. Short distance race e.g. 50 metres 2. Simple Jumps 3. Safety rules in Athletics.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. perform simple athletic activities; 2. explain the health benefits of running, jumping and throwing etc; 3. safety rules in running, jumping and throwing etc.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Demonstrates the events e.g. 50 metres (start from and finish) -jumping (run-up, take off, flight and landing). 2. Explains safety rules. 3. Supervises and corrects practice by pupils.

Students: 1. Observe the teacher’s demonstration in; running (start from and finish) jumping, running(run-up, take off, flight and landing). 2. Practice the event. 3. Mention safety rules.
resources.resources: 1. Playground, 2. Cross-bar, 3. Up right poles 4. Landing pit
resources.assessment: Ask the pupils to: 1. perform simple athletic activities such as running, jumping etc; 2. perform 50 metres dash showing start from and finish; 3. demonstrate basic high jump skills: - run-up - take off - flight - landing; 4. mention safety rules on short distance races (50 metres dash and simple jumps).

resources.title: Games
resources.description: Theme: SPORTS AND GAMES | Content: 1. Local games:  rats and rabbits;  cat and rat;  fire on the mountain etc. 2. Kicking and stopping etc. 3. Safety rules
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. demonstrate the skills of some local games; 2. perform some local games; 3. perform the basic skills in ball games; 4. mention safety rules in games.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the local games to the pupils. 2. Demonstrates the various local games 3. Explains the skills in kicking and stopping. 4. Observes the pupils and offers assistance. 5. List safety rules.

Students: 1. Observe the teacher’s demonstration 2. Practise the skills of the local games. 3. Play the local games. 4. Practise the skills of kicking and stopping. 5. Mention safety rules
resources.resources: Playground, balls etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. demonstrate the skills involved in the local games; 2. perform the local games correctly; 3. perform the skills of ball games e.g. kicking and stopping etc. Correctly; 4. list some safety rules in games.

resources.title: Swimming
resources.description: Theme: SPORTS AND GAMES | Content: 1. Skills for beginners;  Coming into and out of water  Adjusting to the water  Breathing  Turtle float  Face float 2. Safety rules 3. Benefits of swimming
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. mention the preliminary skills of swimming; 2. list some benefits of swimming; 3. list safety rules of swimming.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the preliminary skills. 2. Demonstrates the preliminary skills. 3. Supervises the pupils. 4. Explains safety rules in swimming 5. List benefits of swimming.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher 2. Perform the preliminary skills. 3. Observe safety rules 4. mention benefits of swimming
resources.resources: 1. Swimming pool 2. Whistle 3. Swimming trunk 4. swimming clothe / life jacket etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention the preliminary skills; 2. list some safety rules of swimming; 3. list some benefits of swimming.

resources.title: Health and Hygiene
resources.description: Theme: HEALTH EDUCATION | Content: 1. General body cleanliness in:  washing hands, bathing and care of the skin;  teeth brushing, chewing stick, toothbrush and paste;  cutting of nails;  hair maintenance;  foot wear. 2. Benefits of cleanliness.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain how to wash hands, bath and care for the skin; 2. demonstrate how to brush the teeth; 3. describe how to cut nails; 4. state ways of maintaining foot wears; 5. mention ways of maintaining the hair; 6. Mention benefits of cleanliness.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides the pupils to demonstrate how to wash hands, bathe and brush the teeth. 2. Guides the pupils through discussion on care of nails, hairs, foot wears, clothes and the skin. 3. List the benefits of cleanliness.

Students: 1. Participate and demonstrate how to wash hands, bath and brush the teeth. 2. Participate in discussion on the care for the following: -nails - hairs - foot wears - clothes. 3. Mention some benefits of cleanliness
resources.resources: 1. Charts 2. Posters 3. Sponge 4. Water 5. Scissors/ clippers 6. Chewing stick. 7. Tooth brush and paste. 8. Towels 9. Pomade 10. Slippers/ shoes 11. Stocking 12. Blouses 13. Skirts 14. Shorts
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. describe how to wash hands, bath and care for the skin; 2. demonstrate how to brush the teeth; 3. describe how to cut the nails; 4. mention some ways of maintaining hair, foot wears and clothes; 5. list some benefits of cleanliness.

resources.title: First Aid
resources.description: Theme: HEALTH EDUCATION | Content: 1. Meaning of First Aid. 2. Objectives of First Aid:  arrest bleeding  to save life  prevent injury from becoming worse. 3. Content of First Aid Box.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of First Aid; 2. state the objectives of First Aid; 3. list some contents First Aid Box.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. States the meaning of First Aid. 2. Guides pupils to List and explain some objectives of First Aid. 3. Presents a First Aid Box with its content and guides pupils to identify the contents.

Students: 1. State the meaning of first aid. 2. List objectives of first aid 3. Identify content of First Aid Box
resources.resources: 1. First Aid Box 2. Charts 3. Posters 4. Pictures
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. state what First Aid is; 2. state at least three objectives of First Aid; 3. list, at least, three contents of a First Aid Box.

resources.title: Parts of a computer
resources.description: Theme: BASIC COMPUTER OPERATIONS | Content: 1. Description of a computer 2. Parts of a computer: i. Monitor ii. Keyboard iii. System unit iv. Mouse v. Printer vi. Speakers 3. Drawing of computer parts
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. describe a computer; 2. name parts of a computer; 3. identify computer parts; 4. state the differences between a computer and a television; 5. draw/sketch parts of a computer.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to identify a computer 2. Arranges computer parts on a table 3. Provides the pictures of computer parts and guides pupils to match the pictures with the real objects. 4. Displays the mouse, printer and speakers on the table. 5. Provides the pictures of the mouse, printer and speakers and guides pupils to match the pictures with the real objects.

Students: 1. Identify a computer. 2. Touch and identify the mouse, monitor, printer and speakers. 3. Draw and colour the pictures of the identified parts
resources.resources: 1. Charts 2. Pictures 3. Flash cards 4. Mouse 5. Printer 6. Speakers 7. Pictures 8. Plain paper 9. Colour pencil 10. Keyboard 11. Monitor 12. System unit
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention the differences between a computer and a television; 2. name other parts of a computer e.g. mouse, printer etc; 3. point to the parts of a computer in pictures or on charts; 4. name and colour the picture of computer parts.

resources.title: Uses of Computers
resources.description: Theme: BASIC COMPUTER OPERATIONS | Content: Uses of computer: i. playing games ii. typing of text iii. watching educational films. iv. Storing information, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to state the uses of a computer.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to use the computer to play games, type text, watch educational films, etc. 2. Shows pupils things produced with a computer.

Students: 1. Pupils play games, watch educational films, type text on the computer, etc. 2. Come out in groups of two to examine what the teacher has produced with computer.
resources.resources: 1. Computer 2. Paper 3. Learning software. 4. Printer 5. Items produced with the computer such as drawings, paintings, print-outs, books, etc.
resources.assessment: Ask pupils to mention three uses of a computer

resources.title: Common IT Devices
resources.description: Theme: BASIC CONCEPTS OF IT | Content: 1. Common IT devices:  GSM phones  calculators  Digital wristwatch etc. 2. Description of common IT devices
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify common IT devices; 2. describe common IT devices.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays real objects / pictures of common IT devices. 2. Describes common IT devices.

Students: 1. Touch and identify common IT devices. 2. Draw and colour identified IT devices.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures 2. Chats 3. GSM phones 4. Toy GSM phones 5. Smart phones 6. Colour pencils 7. Plain paper 8. Workbook, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list three IT devices; 2. point to some common IT device on a chart; 3. name and colour some common IT devices in the workbook.

resources.title: The senses
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: 1. Seeing: with eyes. Colours, shapes and sizes of objects in classroom, school and home. 2. Hearing: with ears. Listening to sounds of objects, animals, persons, and imitating sounds. 3. Smelling: with nose. Detecting various odours. 4. Taste: with tongue. Detecting various food items that are sweet, sour, salty and bitter. 5. Touching: with fingers. Detecting various objects by touch, feeling its shape, texture, pressure and temperature. 6. Road users e. g children, cars, Bicycles, animals, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. observe and name colours, shapes and sizes of common objects; 2. identify various sounds made by objects, animals and persons; 3. detect various odours of fruits, food, shoes, dirty socks; etc. 4. detect taste of sweet, sour, salty and bitter food items; 5. identify objects by touching and feeling; 6. describe how correct ways of using the road by each of the users.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Provides and helps pupils to identify: - different colours - different shapes - different sizes. 2. Aides pupils to use coloured pencils and identify colours 3. Makes pupils to listen to and identify various sounds. 4. Guides pupils to recognize something (fruits, food, etc) with characteristic smell. 5. Assists to detect distinctive taste of sweet, sour, salty and bitter tastes. 6. Provides sweet, sour, salty and bitter items to pupils. 7. Provides items of different textures, shapes, temperature and pressure. 8. Assists pupils to identify road users and how to use the roads correctly by each user.

Students: 1. Work with coloured pencils and crayons 2. Collect and identify objects of different shapes and sizes- 3. Identify various sounds. 4. Produce different sounds from their mouth and throat. 5. Describe pleasant and unpleasant smell. 6. Taste sweet, sour, salty and bitter items. 7. Feel or touch their cheeks and heads, tissue paper, touch different types of paper/cardboards 8. Touch cold and warm objects or water. 9. Identify road users and describe correct ways of using the roads.
resources.resources: 1. Coloured pencils and crayon. 2. Wooden blocks of different sizes, shapes and colours. 3. Charts and models. 4. School bell, flute, other wind instrument. 5. Recorded sounds of birds, frog, cat, etc. 6. Fruits-banana, oranges, mango. 7. Flower, shoes, dirty socks, etc. 8. Sugar, honey, salt, bitter leaf/kola. 9. Tissue paper. 10. Rough and smooth cardboard. 11. Cold/hot, warm water. 12. Video and Charts on road usage. 13. Pictures of ifferent types of roads.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify and match objects based on colours, shape, and size; 2. identify and describe sounds made by different objects, animals and persons; 3. associate odours with specific pleasant and unpleasant smell; 4. state the taste of different substances; 5. distinguish between rough and coarse objects, cold and hot, etc; 6. name three road users; 7. describe various ways of using the road.

resources.title: Soil Types
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: 1. Types of soil - clay - sandy - loamy 2. Properties of soil types
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. mention different types of soil; 2. observe and describe the physical properties of soil types.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Identifies suitable sites in the school compound from where different soil types can be collected. 2. Takes pupils to the identified sites in the school to collect soil samples. 3. Guides pupils to name the different soil types. 4. Guides pupils to observe and describe the colour, texture and particles size of the soil samples.

Students: 1. Collect soil samples in the school or home environment. 2. Observe and describe the colour, texture and particles size of the soil samples. 3. Place some soil samples in a container, add water and stir. 4. Mould with wet sand and clay. 5. Compare clay soil and sandy soil.
resources.resources: 1. Samples of garden soil (clay, loamy and sandy soils) 2. Hand lens 3. Sieve 4. Filter paper 5. Containers 6. Funnel 7. Water 8. Hoe or shovel
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify and name soil types as: loamy, clay and sandy soil; 2. describe the physical properties of the soil types.

resources.title: Air
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: 1. Floating in the air 2. Things that float in air (paper kites, blown balloons, etc.)
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. observe and identify things that float in air; 2. make things float in air.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to name things that float in air. 2. Guides pupils to make paper kites. 3. Score the kites thatpupilsmake.

Students: 1. Throw things into the air and identify those that float, and those that do not. 2. Make and fly paper kites.
resources.resources: 1. Balloons 2. Old newspapers 3. Thread 4. Gum 5. Sticks 6. Strings 7. Stones 8. Pencils
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. name five things that float in air; 2. make and fly paper kites.

resources.title: Water
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: Floating and sinking in water.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify things that float or sink in water; 2. demonstrate how to make objects float or sink in water.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to identify objects that: - float in water - sink in water. 2. Demonstrates to pupils some ways of making objects: - float in water e.g. stone placed on inflated balloon, human being swimming with the aid of a life jacket or calabash; - sinking in water (e.g. tying a stone to a feather, cork, etc. 3. Initiates and guides class discussion on other ways of making things float or sink in water.

Students: 1. Name things that float in water. 2. Observe the demonstrations. 3. Make things to float in water. 4. Make things to sink in water.
resources.resources: 1. Balloons 2. Dry wood 3. Meter rule 4. Piece of iron 5. Stone 6. Thread 7. Feathers 8. Cork 9. Picture of people in swimming pools using life jackets (inflated wears) or in river staying on top of calabashes
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. name three things each that float or sink in water; 2. make things to float or sink in water.

resources.title: Colours
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: Use of colours
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to use colours to identify and beautify objects.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to identify objects through colours (living & non-living things). 2. Guides pupils to discuss uses of colours

Students: Colour objects
resources.resources: 1. Papers 2. Crayons 3. Coloured pens 4. colour charts 5. Lego set/beads. 6. Dyes
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. colour two types of objects; 2. use Lego of different colours to construct common objects.

resources.title: Plants
resources.description: Theme: LIVING AND NON LIVING THINGS | Content: 1. Plants in the school compound 2. Features of plants: - shape - size - colour - texture 3. Common uses of plants in the locality (for food, beautification, building, furniture, shade, medicines.)
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify and name some common plants in the school compound; 2. trace the leaves of some of the plants on Plastercine or clay, where available; 3. prepare a press of common plants; 4. observe and identify features of common plants in their school compound; 5. group plants according to their common features; 6. group plants according to their uses; 7. describe common uses of plants.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Identifies suitable place in the surrounding for pupils to visit. 2. Guides pupils to observe and collect common plants. 3. Guides pupils to prepare a plant for preservation 4. Initiate class discussions which would enable pupils to: - identify features of the plants - group the plants based on their features 5. Through class discussion: - guides pupils to state the uses of plants - groups plants according to their uses.

Students: 1. Participate in site visits 2. Observe and collect some common pants 3. Print some plant parts e.g. leaves 4. Prepare a print- press of common plants. 5. Identify features of plants 6. Group plants according to their features. 7. Group plants according to their uses.
resources.resources: 1. Specimen of local plants 2. Drawing books 3. Pencils 4. Crayons 5. Cello-tapes 6. Plastercine 7. Clay 8. Workbooks
resources.assessment: Ask pupils to: 1. name five common plants in the school; 2. trace the leaves of some plants; 3. prepare and display print press; 4. mention the features of the plants in their locality; 5. state the uses of plants; 6. group plants according to their common features 7. group plants according to their uses.

resources.title: Animals
resources.description: Theme: LEARNING ABOUT OUR ENVIRONMENT | Content: 1. Animals in the school compound (flies, butterflies, earthworms etc.) 2. Features of the animals found in the school compound. 3. Behaviour of animals. 4. Animals and road safety.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify common animals in the school compound; 2. collect and preserve some animals in the school compound; 3. observe and name the features of common animals in the school compound; 4. use the observable features to group the animals found in the school compound; 5. observe and describe the behaviour of animals; 6. demonstrate correct way of: - crossing the road; - walking along the road leading
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses pictures and charts to guide pupils to identify common animals in the school compound. 2. Demonstrates the correct method of collecting animals for preservation. 3. Guides pupils to: - identify the features of the animals, - group animals using observable features. 4. Initiates and guides class discussion on the behaviour of animals e.g. movement, feeding etc. 5. Demonstrate crossing and walking along the road.

Students: 1. Identify animals in their school compound. 2. Collects harmless animals in the school compound. 3. Observe, group and describe features of preserved animals 4. Make drawings of some animals. 5. Participate in class discussion on animals 6. Mimic the sound of some animals.
resources.resources: 1. Charts and pictures of animals. 2. Specimen of animals. 3. Insect nets/baskets 4. Specimen bottles and jars 5. Preservative (e.g. formalin) 6. Workbook 7. Live animal 8. Petri dishes 9. Lids of cans 10. Plastic plates
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. name some common animals in the school compound; 2. collect and display common animals in the school compound; 3. describe the features of animals; 4. group animals based on observed features; 5. describe the behaviour of animals; 6. describe correct ways of: - walking along the road, - Crossing the road.

resources.title: Clay
resources.description: Theme: UNDERSTANDING BASIC TECHNOLOGY | Content: 1. Preparation of clay for moulding. 2. Moulding with clay.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. prepare clay for moulding; 2. use clay for moulding.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains stages of using and preserving clay 2. Assists pupils in preparation 3. Assists pupils in moulding objects with clay

Students: Make objects using clay
resources.resources: 1. Clay 2. Water 3. Heat
resources.assessment: Ask pupils to: 1. prepare clay for moulding; 2. mould objects using clay.

resources.title: Forms of Energy (Sound)
resources.description: Theme: YOU AND ENERGY | Content: 1. Forms of energy. 2. Sound energy: - things that produce sounds; - musical instruments.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify different forms of energy; 2. identify different sounds; 3. name some instruments that produce sounds; 4. make local instruments that produce sounds; 5. make different kinds of sounds with the instruments they made.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to identify different forms of energy. 2. Discusses sound and leads pupils to identify sounds. 3. Uses the chart to guide pupils to identify different instruments that produce sounds. 4. Guides pupils to make musical instruments from local materials.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions. 2. Make sounds with different parts of their bodies (e.g. feet, hands, mouth. 3. Identify and name instruments that produce sound. 4. Construct local musical instruments from available materials. 5. Play games with sound using the musical instrument they made.
resources.resources: 1. A chart showing some musical instruments 2. Bamboo Stem; 3. Paw-paw stalk 4. Knife 5. String 6. Some musical instruments e.g. talking drum, mouth organ, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention the different forms of energy; 2. identify sounds made from different sources; 3. list three instruments that produce sound; 4. make sounds with different parts of their bodies; 5. make local musical instruments and make melodies with them.

resources.title: Moving our body parts
resources.description: Theme: BASIC MOVEMENTS | Content: 1. Movement Patterns: - Shooting and heading. - Bending and stretching - People matching - Jogging - Galloping - skipping 2. Movement of animals. 3. Movement by machines. 4. Safety rules.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. demonstrate correct movement patterns of shooting and heading; 2. perform basic movement such as bending, stretching; 3. imitate movement and sound made by people, animals and machine around them; 4. identify safety rules in shooting, heading, bending and stretching.
resources.activities:

resources.title: Storage devices
resources.description: Theme: BASIC CONCEPTS OF IT | Content: 1. Meaning of storage devices 2. Types of computer storage devices: -flash disk -hard disk -compact disk, etc 3. Difference between storage drive and disk 4. Uses/functions of storage devices 5. Care of storage devices
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the term storage device; 2. identify types of computer storage devices; 3. uses/functions of storage devices; 4. mention ways of caring for storage devices.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays and explain a system unit on the table. 2. Shows pupils types of storage devices 3. Explains more on hard disk because it cannot easily be seen. 4. Guides pupils to state difference between storage disk and storage drive 5. Guides pupils to list types of storage devices and writes short notes on them. 6. Guides pupils to identify different types of computer storage devices. 7. Guides pupils to mention ways of caring for storage devices.

Students: 1. Examine the storage devices on display. 2. Copy notes from the chalkboard on storage devices. 3. Ask questions about Hard disk 4. Make attempts to mention types of storage devices. 5. Make attempts to state difference between storage disk and storage drive. 6. Make attempts to mention uses/functions of storage devices. 7. Make attempts to list cares of storage devices.
resources.resources: 1. Floppy disk 2. Compact disk. 3. DVD 4. Hard disk 5. Flash disk.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify and mention three types of storage devices; 2. mention three differences between storage disk and storage drive; 3. state three uses of storage devices; 4. mention three ways of caring for storage devices.
